# Lola Walkthrough — Guest-Legibility Audit (2026-06-20)

## Verdict

Guest surfaces are **mostly usable but consistently hostile to an older guest's eyes and fingers.** The good news: contrast under the couple's mood-board palette is solved by construction (`site-palette.ts` pins `ink` to obsidian and only tints `paper` above 0.82 luminance — the historic cream-on-cream veil bug cannot recur), the just-shipped veil reveal (PR #1872) is a model for size + contrast + gesture-fallback, and the core jobs rarely require a login on the personal-link path. The bad news: a single failure pattern dominates — **load-bearing text and controls rendered at 7–12px in `font-mono uppercase tracking-[…]`**, where the thing the guest most needs (the table number, the "Not me" button, the "Save photo" icon, the seal-open instruction) is among the *smallest, faintest* elements on screen. The **worst surface is Seat finding** — three HIGH findings where the entire payoff (the table number, the map's "You're here" badge) renders at 7–14px — closely followed by the **Papic gallery** (the two actions an elder came to do, save-a-photo and remove-a-wrong-one, are both sub-44px icon-only controls) and the **QR join/claim flow** (a hard account-creation wall plus 17px-tall recovery links). The single most common failure is **sub-14px actionable copy in wide-tracked uppercase mono**, present on all 7 surfaces.

## Top fixes (highest-leverage first)

1. **Seat finding — `name-search.tsx:137-139`** — The table number, the whole point of the finder and the most common elder job, renders at the *same* 14px as the guest's own name in a small chip. → Make `match.table_label` the largest element on screen: `text-4xl font-bold text-success-800` on its own line under the name.
2. **Seat finding — `wayfinding-map.tsx:184, 190-193, 128-130`** — In-map text is unreadable: table labels 9px, "You're here" confirmation badge 7px, "Entrance" 8px. An elder confirms their table by color glow alone. → Either lift target-table labels to ≥13px and drop the uppercase/tracking on the "You're here" badge, or treat the map as positional-only and lean on the existing large `text-2xl` headline caption.
3. **Papic gallery / Day-of — `save-photo-button.tsx:26-37`** — The primary "keep my photo" action is an icon-only ~20px corner dot (`p-1`, 12px icon, `sr-only` label) on a 3-up grid tile. The elder can't see or hit it. → ≥44px hit target with a *visible* "Save" word, or a full-width "Save to phone" button under an enlarged photo.
4. **Papic gallery / Day-of — `[slug]/page.tsx:2144-2156, 2149`** — The "Not me" correction button is a 9px label in an ~18px chip jammed into the corner of an 80px (`grid-cols-4`) thumbnail — sub-44px and unreadable, yet the helper copy explicitly tells guests to use it. → Tap-to-open the photo, then a full-width "This isn't me — remove it" row at ≥16px / ≥44px.
5. **QR join — `join/[eventId]/page.tsx:86-108`** — `/join` forces email/password account creation before an elder can confirm she's coming, even though `/[slug]/redeem` already proves a cookie-session needs no login. → Let a scanned-QR guest join via the same cookie-session pattern; if an account is truly needed, lead with a passwordless email-code path and demote "Create account."
6. **QR verify — `join/[eventId]/verify/page.tsx:109-119`** — The OTP recovery links ("Resend it" / "Ask the couple") are bare 14px text links with a ~17px tappable height — the hardest things to hit at the exact moment the code didn't arrive. → Give both real button hit areas: `min-h-[44px]`, full-width, `py-2.5`.
7. **Save-the-Date film — `save-the-date-film.tsx:955-959 + rigid-stage.tsx:411-432`** — The whole experience is gesture-driven with chrome deliberately stripped, and there is **no rendered cue telling the guest how to advance**; indefinite-hold beats (video, "add to calendar") can silently dead-end. On rigid openings the gating instruction is an 11px wide-tracked line and the open step is an undiscoverable scrub. → Port the veil's shipped pattern (`reveal-overlay.tsx:192-205`): a persistent ≥14px "Swipe up to continue" pill on a contrast scrim, plus a tap fallback so the film and the seal-open can never strand an elder. Raise the seal/open instructions to ≥16px.
8. **Guest email — `alaala/assignments/actions.ts:155-158`** — The Kwento story-assignment email is plain-text with **no link, button, or URL** — the one job (go add your story) is literally unreachable from the inbox. → Render via `renderBrandedEmail()` with a single CTA (`Add my message`, `${appUrl}/${slug}`), or at minimum append the full tappable URL.
9. **Systemic — cream/gold-on-light & dimmed-grey actionable copy (~9 places)** — Sub-14px or ≤55%-opacity text on copy a guest *must* read recurs across surfaces: RSVP saved-tile `bg-terracotta text-cream` (skinnable accent as background, no contrast guarantee — `page.tsx:2590-2592`), gold `terracotta` DEFAULT #C5A059 eyebrows on near-white cream (~2:1, `find-seat/page.tsx:66-68`, `join-shell.tsx:20`, `papic/claim:32-34`), and ink/45–55 instruction copy on find-seat, welcome, and guest-hub. → Run the existing auto-contrast pass (`site-palette.ts:264-275`) on any accent-as-background; never use the gold DEFAULT for small text; floor instructional copy at 14px / ink-70.

## Systemic patterns — lint guardrail vs one-off

Two failure classes account for nearly every finding and should become **automated lint rules**, not per-file fixes:

1. **Sub-size actionable text.** The `font-mono text-[7px|8px|9px|10px|11px] uppercase tracking-[0.14em–0.3em]` eyebrow/label pattern is everywhere (e.g. `guest-hub-card.tsx:190/216/236/261/285/303`, `page.tsx:2124/2128/2149/3104/3150`, `rigid-stage.tsx:411/428`, `wayfinding-map.tsx:184/190/128/89`, `std-themes.ts:64`). Add a **min-size LINT guardrail** that flags any `text-[≤13px]` on elements outside a `decorative`/brand allowlist, and especially blocks `text-[≤11px]` on anything with an `onClick`/`href`/`aria-label`. Pair it with a **44px tap-target rule** for interactive controls (`save-photo-button`, "Not me" chip, OTP recovery links, RSVP quick-link pills, selfie checkbox).

2. **Accent-as-background contrast.** The current `site-palette.ts` AA pass guarantees accent only *as text on paper* — it does **not** cover accent used as a *background* under cream/white text (`RsvpWidget` selected tile, `page.tsx:2590-2592`). This is the one place the contrast story is incomplete and a real wash-out risk on light mood-board palettes. Make "skinnable accent used as `bg-*` under a fixed light foreground" a **lint-flagged pattern** routed through the existing `FILM_CREAM/FILM_INK` best-contrast logic.

**One-off (don't lint):** the jargon items ("RSVP", "tagged", "match you to their guest list", "claim/seat"), the gesture-cue gap on the STD film, the `/join` account wall, and the Kwento email's missing link are judgment fixes, not mechanical ones — handle them individually. The gold `terracotta` DEFAULT (#C5A059) on near-white is borderline systemic; if it keeps appearing on instructional copy, fold "accent DEFAULT on `bg-cream` for `text-[≤14px]`" into the contrast lint too.
